# MNCS-native Journal decision core (`mncs.family.journal.v1`)

**Status:** implemented, executed, validated on five backends.
**Module:** `library/family/journal.mncs` (Profile 0.10).
**Corpus:** `examples/execution/journal-corpus.json` (35 cases, generated by
`scripts/gen_journal_corpus.py`).
**Tests:** `crates/mncs-cli/tests/journal.rs`.

## What this module is

The executable policy half of the Journal architecture. Host orchestrators
(Atlas maintainer, Forge, Fabric clients) gather facts — repository state,
Action results, evidence receipts, digests — and must obtain admission
verdicts by executing this module. Reimplementing these verdicts host-side
would launder authority, exactly as `mncs.family.coherence.v01` already
requires for family promotion.

Governing principle, enforced by construction:

```text
Models may interpret.
Validators may attest.
Policy decides.
```

## What it decides

- `gate_admit(EvidenceTally) -> Status`: PASS only when every required
  evidence item is satisfied, current, and integrity-clean. Stale or
  integrity-failed evidence is FAIL; incomplete but well-formed evidence is
  UNKNOWN. Never maps UNKNOWN to PASS.
- `admission_decision(AdmissionCase) -> AdmissionVerdict`: Admit only on
  validator PASS plus gate PASS, with no duplicate and no model-only claim.
  Duplicates and model-only claims are rejected even when every tally
  passes (reasons 3 and 4).
- `trust_transition(TrustLevel, TrustEvent, Status) -> TrustTransition`:
  stepwise `Observed -> LocallyProven -> IndependentlyConfirmed ->
  CommonsPromoted` upgrades need PASS; skips hold (reason 1); gate-refused
  upgrades hold (reason 2); `LegacyUnattested` never upgrades (reason 3,
  quarantine); `CommonsPromoted` is terminally stable.
- `chain_ok(parent, previous) -> bool`: delegates to
  `mncs.core.lineage.v1.valid_root_or_successor`. Genesis root plus
  successor links pass; edits, reorders, and forks are Conflict.
- `model_may_admit(ModelOpinion) -> bool`: constantly false. Model hints
  (`model_hint_duplicate/sensitive/worthy`) are observable facts the host
  may carry into a case record or redaction review, never admission inputs.
- `may_render_public(Sensitivity, Status) -> bool`: only gate-PASS events
  render, and security-detail events additionally require redaction review.

## Vocabulary

`EventKind` is a bounded 16-variant enum (capability added/proven/
regressed, RFC advanced/completed, backend conformant/regressed, stdlib
expanded, pressure discovered/resolved, security finding/resolved, Commons
promoted, project migrated, release created, architecture changed). Routine
churn has no code: what is not one of these is not journal-worthy. The
language has no string type, so kinds, levels, and reason codes are finite
codes; the host string table in the Atlas event schema is boundary glue.

## Validation

`journal_gates_pass_on_every_backend` runs all 35 corpus cases on
`mncs-research-bytecode`, `mncs-portable-wasm-mvp`, `mncs-c11`,
`mncs-llvm-ir`, and `mncs-cranelift`. `journal_model_opinion_never_admits`
pins the model-authority boundary on the reference backend.

## What this module is not

It stores nothing, signs nothing, and renders nothing. Canonical JSON
serialization, sha256 chaining, ed25519 attestation, append-only storage,
and HTML projection live in the Atlas event log (`mncs-atlas`,
`docs/JOURNAL_EVENTS.md`), which treats this module's verdicts as the
admission authority and fails closed to UNKNOWN when the MNCS toolchain is
unavailable.
